comparator_v1_issue: No issue-level universe; pair labels contained eight positives and no explicit negative pairs.

pattern_false_positives.compact_definition: Off-chain components observe specific on-chain state/events and react outside the blockchain; outbound information flow.
pattern_false_positives.keywords: contract.on('EventName'|ethers.js event listener|web3.eth.subscribe('logs'|off-chain relayer listening to contract events|event-driven off-chain worker
pattern_false_positives.llm_evidence_examples: ["It's very welcome on our end (Phala Network), because we extensively rely on events to notify our offchain systems. I think it's also useful for indexers like SubQuery and Subscan.", "Payment evaluation happens automatically, but with a few minutes delay. When payment is detected, an Accept Review is automatically placed on the PR"]

pattern_false_positives.compact_definition: Transfer and initialize source-chain state on the destination chain during migration.
pattern_false_positives.keywords: importState() on target chain|bootstrapState() from migration snapshot|state migration initializer contract
pattern_false_positives.llm_evidence_examples: ["the test contract isn't in the `persisted_accounts` list during initialization and as such isn't migrated to zksync. This causes it to be incorrectly migrated to an empty code account when a evm fork is encountered.", "Migration can assume max severity for all pending slashes"]

pattern_false_positives.compact_definition: A creator contract creates new instances of other smart contracts; deployment primitives alone are insufficient.
pattern_false_positives.llm_evidence_examples: ["Uniswap uses CREATE2 to determine the address of a pool. The advantage is that the address of a pool with two specific tokens and a specific fee tier is deterministic and computable wether the pool is deployed or not."]

pattern_false_positives.compact_definition: Map a decentralized identifier (DID) to off-chain attributes in a contract; private-key possession proves control.
pattern_false_positives.keywords: DID registry smart contract|resolveDID(string did)|did:ethr method|ERC-1056 EthereumDIDRegistry|DID document storage on-chain
pattern_false_positives.llm_evidence_examples: ["No native ENS support to resolve or reverse resolve `.eth` address to ethereum address, text records (include avatar, email, etc), ipfs/arweave/skynet hash (for websites)"]

pattern_false_positives.compact_definition: Forward calls to a replaceable implementation contract to upgrade logic while retaining the public address.
pattern_false_positives.keywords: delegatecall-based proxy|EIP-1167 minimal proxy clone|TransparentUpgradeableProxy|UUPSUpgradeable|ERC-1967 implementation slot|upgradeTo(address newImplementation)
pattern_false_positives.llm_evidence_examples: ["Instead of setting approval for the exchange contract I have to approve it for the assigned proxy? | Yep! First you should make sure that there is a deployed proxy for that address. If there isn't one yet, you'll have to call the `WyvernProxyRegistry.registerProxy()`"]

pattern_false_positives.compact_definition: Assign roles to addresses and enforce different permissions for each role (RBAC).
The application constructs a transaction; the user manually confirms and signs it with a browser wallet.
